f9f591c7139b1a46232d5e944469f2579542d648.summary: Hybrid Analysis sandbox page for an unnamed Windows sample (hash prefix 5d631d774016…) with a score of 100/100 and a malicious rating of 100%. Static analysis and ML by CrowdStrike flagged it with relatively high confidence, and many antivirus engines flagged it. Listed behaviours include a YARA match, unusual PE entropy, registry key monitoring, reads of terminal service keys, process hooking and suspicious API imports. No malware family, actor, CVE, sector or country is named.

f9015ec340e025c16963e9b7cef4cbc3f4101ca7.summary: Group-IB describes JadeProx, a China-nexus operation found through an exposed staging server and active against targets in Vietnam, Malaysia, Hong Kong, Honduras and Venezuela. It centres on the TriBack Loader, which uses DLL sideloading with signed binaries to deliver AdaptixC2 or Beagle. Lures include Claude-themed software, a fake Honduran beverage-company statement and a fake Venezuelan municipal tax portal that collects credentials. Post-exploitation tooling includes iox, suo5, Neo-reGeorg, nuclei and fscan. The report says no single group matches the full picture, so it tracks the…

f947718c75929c5f5807f0f778453ca1453464c6.summary: SentinelLABS reports an intrusion into NPO Mashinostroyeniya, a sanctioned Russian missile engineering organisation, flagged internally in May 2022. It links a Windows backdoor, OpenCarrot, to the Lazarus Group, and a compromised Linux email server to ScarCruft. The authors attribute the intrusion to threat actors independently associated with North Korea with a high level of confidence, but say they cannot determine how the two actors relate. Command infrastructure was hosted on VPS providers and active from November 2021 until it was paused after discovery.

hedges: The authors cannot determine the nature of the relationship between the two threat actors.
The initial access method and the implant on the email server could not be confirmed at discovery.
The compilation timestamp could have been manipulated, but is judged likely authentic.
Domain-name similarity alone is superficial and not strong enough for direct clustering.
Shared infrastructure with an unrelated group is assessed as reused low-cost VPS hosting, not related activity.
The ScarCruft and BlueNoroff links rest on shared infrastructure and tooling; the BlueNoroff link is lower-confidence.
Shared resources, or several independent actors tasked to the same target, are acknowledged as possibilities, not confirmed.
The leaked email collection is suggested to be accidental, so its origin is unclear.
